issues.description: The problem statement's UML and textual specification declare the method checkOrderReady() as returning void, but the provided solution implements checkOrderReady() returning a boolean. This mismatch in the method signature for the same conceptual operation (attempting to serve queued orders) can confuse students: the problem text and diagram suggest a procedure-only method (no return value), while the solution exposes a return value indicating whether any orders were served.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution method to match the problem (public void checkOrderReady()) and keep internal behavior the same, or (B) update the problem statement and UML to declare checkOrderReady(): boolean and document the return semantics (e.g., returns true if at least one order was served). Prefer option (A) if the exercise expects a procedure-only method to match the specification.
